questions.stem: For complex ion $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ what is the charge on metal and shape of complex respectively?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Ni^{2+}} \rightarrow 3d^{8}$
$\mathrm{Cl^-}$ ligand is weak field ligand and hybridisation is $sp^{3}$. Shape of complex is tetrahedral.

questions.stem:
Compare boiling point of given solutions
(i) $10^{-4}\ \mathrm{M\ NaCl}$
(ii) $10^{-3}\ \mathrm{M\ NaCl}$
(iii) $10^{-2}\ \mathrm{M\ NaCl}$
(iv) $10^{-4}\ \mathrm{M}$ urea
questions.solution:
Higher the elevation in boiling point, higher will be the boiling point
$\Delta T_b \propto i \times m$
For urea $i = 1$
For NaCl $i = 2$
Boiling point order $\mathrm{III > II > I > IV}$

questions.stem: Which of the following has maximum size out of $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{F^{-}}$, $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$?
questions.solution:
For isoelectronic species, more the negative charge more will be the size, also more the positive charge smaller will be the size.
The correct order of ionic size is :
$\mathrm{Al^{3+} < Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{-}}$

questions.stem:
Compare crystal field splitting energy($\Delta$) for given complexes
(i) $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$
(ii) $\mathrm{[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{+2}}$s
(iii) $\mathrm{K_4[Fe(SCN)_6]}$
(iv) $\mathrm{[Fe(en)_3]Cl_3}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]} \Rightarrow d^{6} \Rightarrow$ SFL,
$\mathrm{K_2[Cu(NH_3)_4]} \Rightarrow d^{9} \Rightarrow dsp^{2}$
$\mathrm{K_4[Fe(SCN)_6]} \Rightarrow d^{6} \Rightarrow$ WFL
$\mathrm{[Fe(en)_3]Cl_3} \Rightarrow d^{5} \Rightarrow$ SFL
Splitting energy $\propto$ Strength of ligand $\propto$ Charge of CA.
$\Delta_{sp} > \Delta_{o}$
$\mathrm{II > I > IV > III}$

questions.stem: An electron of $\mathrm{He^{+}}$ is present in $3^{rd}$ excited state. Find its de-Broglie wavelength.
questions.solution:
$n\lambda = 2\pi r$
For $3^{rd}$ excited state, $n = 4$
$$4\lambda = 2 \times \pi \times a_{\circ}\frac{n^{2}}{z}$$
$$4\lambda = 2 \times \pi \times 0.529\frac{16}{2}\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$$
$\lambda = 2 \times 3.14 \times 0.529 \times 2\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}} = 6.64\ \mathrm{\mathring{A}}$

questions.stem:
Given : $\mathrm{NH_2COONH_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g) + CO_2(g)}$
If the partial pressure of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas at equilibrium is 0.4 atm and the total pressure is 1 atm, then the value of $K_p$ at the same temperature is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{NH_2COONH_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 2NH_3(g) + CO_2(g)}$
Total pressure at equilibrium = 1.0 atm
Partial pressure of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ at equilibrium = 0.4 atm
$\therefore$ Partial pressure of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ at equilibrium = 0.6 atm
$K_p = (p_{NH_3})^{2}(p_{CO_2})$
$= (0.6)^{2}(0.4)$
$= 0.144\ \mathrm{atm^{3}}$

questions.stem: $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas is taken at 1 atm, 273K. Now it is allowed to pass through 0.1 M $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ aq. solution. questions.solution:
g meq of $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ = 2 × gm eq of HCl
$$0.1 \times \frac{V_{mL}}{1000} \times 2 = 2 \times 0.1 \times \frac{40}{1000} \times 1$$

questions.stem: In a closed insulated container, a liquid is stirred with a paddle to increase the temperature, which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
In closed insulated container a liquid stirred with a paddle to increase the temperature, it behaves as an adiabatic container, $q = 0$
From FLOT
$\Delta U = q + w$; $q = 0$
$\Delta E = w$ (but not zero)

questions.stem: In Carius method 180 mg of organic compound gives 143.5 mg of AgCl. Find the percentage of Cl in the organic compound. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Mass of organic compound = 180 mg
Mass of AgCl = 143.5 mg
Mass of Cl $= \frac{143.5}{143.5} \times 35.5$ mg
$= 35.5$ mg
Percentage of Cl in the organic compound
$$= \frac{35.5 \times 100}{180}$$
$= 19.72\% \simeq 20\%$

questions.stem: Two ampere current is allowed to pass through molten $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ for 30 min. Find the mass (in mg) of aluminium deposited at cathode. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
Total charge passed $= 2 \times 30 \times 60$ C
Number of Faradays passed $= \frac{2 \times 30 \times 60}{96500}$ F
Equivalents of Al deposited $= \frac{36}{965}$
Mass of Al deposited $= \frac{36 \times 9}{965}$ g
$= \frac{36 \times 9 \times 1000}{965}$ mg
$= 335.75$ mg
$\simeq 336$ mg
